subject.title: Slack durable ingress drain stalls during long hybrid exec/process turns; other conversations delayed minutes with zero main-lane wait

question: Should Slack durable ingress preserve a monitor-wide wait-for-idle barrier, or should the shared drain repump independent claimed lanes while an already adopted turn remains active?
rationale: The answer sets the ordering and admission contract for Slack and potentially other durable channel adapters; the current report and the related thread report support a common mechanism but do not establish the intended cross-lane semantics.

options.title: Admit independent lanes concurrently
options.body: Remove or narrow the monitor-wide idle barrier so ready unrelated lanes can be claimed and dispatched while preserving per-lane ordering.

options.title: Preserve global barrier
options.body: Keep monitor-wide serialization and document it as an intentional delivery-order tradeoff, accepting delayed unrelated Slack conversations during long turns.

recommendation.title: Admit independent lanes concurrently
recommendation.body: Remove or narrow the monitor-wide idle barrier so ready unrelated lanes can be claimed and dispatched while preserving per-lane ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: Their durable-ingress design work is the strongest available routing signal for the queue, claim, and adoption contract.
